summary:
I have found the needle and fixed the race condition.

### Cause of the Issue
The application was using a non-atomic read-modify-write pattern:
```javascript
const current = await client.get(COUNTER_KEY);
const value = parseInt(current || "0", 10);
const newValue = value + 1;
await client.set(COUNTER_KEY, newValue.toString());
```
Under concurrency, multiple requests read the same value and incremented it to the same new value, causing lost writes.

### Solution Applied
We replaced the non-atomic block with the Redis atomic `incr` command:
```javascript
const newValue = await client.incr(COUNTER_KEY);
```

### Verification
Running `test.sh` now successfully passes:
```
Firing 100 concurrent increments...
Expected: 100
Got:      100
PASS: Counter is correct
```
